classification.difficultyReason: Find the hypotenuse, compute SA, then reason why scaling the length does not scale the total; similar demand to p17-q6.

content.prompt: The length of this triangular prism is $8$ cm.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the surface area of the prism.

answer.worked:
Let $c$ be the missing side of the triangular end.
$$\begin{align*}c^2&=5^2+12^2\\c&=13\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{ends}}&=2\left(\frac{5\times12}{2}\right)=60\\A_{\text{rectangles}}&=(5+12+13)\times8=240\\A&=60+240=300\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: The length of the prism is tripled to $24$ cm. Find its new surface area.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Explain why the new surface area is not three times the original surface area.

answer.short: The rectangular areas triple, but the two triangular ends keep their combined area of $60\text{ cm}^2$.
answer.worked: Three times the original surface area would triple the triangular ends as well: $3(300)-2(60)=780\text{ cm}^2$. Only the rectangular face areas triple.
